title.full: Earnings Per Share, Growth This Year
title.description: EPS growth this year. Earnings Per Share = Net Income / Number of Shares Outstanding.

title.full: Earnings Per Share, Growth Next Year
title.description: EPS growth estimated next year. Earnings Per Share = Net Income / Number of Shares Outstanding.

title.full: Earnings Per Share, Growth Quarter Over Quarter
title.description:
EPS is the portion of a company's profit allocated to each outstanding share of common stock. EPS serves as an indicator of a company's profitability.

Quarter over quarter growth.
Earnings Per Share growth over past 12 months compared to prior year.

title.full: Earnings Per Share, Growth Past 3 Years
title.description: EPS annual growth over past 3 years. Earnings Per Share = Net Income / Number of Shares Outstanding.

title.full: Earnings Per Share, Growth Past 5 Years
title.description: EPS annual growth over past 5 years. Earnings Per Share = Net Income / Number of Shares Outstanding.

title.full: Earnings Per Share, Growth Next 5 Years
title.description: EPS annual growth estimated next 5 years. Earnings Per Share = Net Income / Number of Shares Outstanding.
Sales growth comparing most recent quarter to same quarter last year.
Sales growth over past 12 months compared to prior year.
Sales annual growth over past 3 years.
Sales annual growth over past 5 years.
Company's EPS and/or Revenue compared to analyst estimates.
Net Income divided by Total Assets. Measures how efficiently a company generates profit from its assets.
Net Income divided by Shareholders' Equity. Measures how efficiently a company generates profit from equity.
Net Income divided by Invested Capital. Measures how efficiently a company generates profit from the capital invested in its business.
Current Assets divided by Current Liabilities. A liquidity measure showing the company's ability to meet short-term obligations.
(Current Assets - Inventory - Prepaids) divided by Current Liabilities. Liquidity measure showing company's ability to meet short-term obligations with its most liquid assets.
Ratio of Long Term Debt to Shareholders' Equity. Measures company's financial leverage.
Ratio of Total Debt to Shareholders' Equity. Measures company's financial leverage.
Percentage of revenue remaining as gross profit after deducting the cost of goods sold. Measures profit above what it costs the company to produce its goods or services.
Percentage of revenue remaining as operating income after operating expenses are subtracted. Measures profitability to a company's core business.
Percentage of revenue remaining as net income after all expenses, taxes, interest, and costs are deducted. Measures bottom-line profitability.
Percentage of earnings paid out as dividends.
Percentage of shares owned by insiders and management.
Six-month change in insider ownership.
Percentage of shares owned by institutional investors.
Three-month change in institutional ownership.
Rate of return for a given stock.
Rate of return for a given stock.
Statistical measure of how much a security's price fluctuates over time, often expressed as the size or dispersion of its returns.
Momentum oscillator that measures the speed and magnitude of recent price changes to indicate whether a security is overbought or oversold.
Difference between yesterday's Close price and today's Open price, where the opening price does not overlap the prior day's trading range.
Average closing price over the previous 20 trading days.
Average closing price over the previous 50 trading days.
Average closing price over the previous 200 trading days.
Difference between previous Close price and Current price.
Difference between today's Open price and Current price.
Highest and lowest price over previous 20 days, and how far current stock price is from those levels.
Highest and lowest price over previous 50 days, and how far current stock price is from those levels.
Highest and lowest price over previous 52 weeks (1 year), and how far current stock price is from those levels.
Highest and lowest price in stock's history, and how far current stock price is from those levels.
Chart patterns that may signal a reversal or continuation of trend.
Candlestick pattern on the daily candle (bar). Candlestick is a visual representation of Open, High, Low, Close.
A measure of a stock's price volatility compared to the overall market. S&P 500 has a Beta of 1. Positive Beta = stock is correlated with the market. Negative Beta = stock is negatively correlated.

A measure of stock volatility. The Average True Range is an exponential moving average (14-days) of the True Ranges. The range of a day's trading is high-low, True Range extends it to yesterday's closing price if it was outside of today's range, True Range = max(high, closeprev) - min(low, closeprev).
The current stock price in after-hours trading.
% change between regular trading closing price and after-hours price.
Date of most recent news related to the company.
